6. The accused-persons being absconding they could not be examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on the closure of the evidence of the prosecution. 

 7. After trial on hearing the learned Advocates for both the sides and on perusal and on analysis of the evidence on record and so also on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, the learned trial judge found the accused-persons guilty of the charge as brought against them and accordingly, convicted and sentenced the accused-persons by the impugned judgment and order as aforesaid. 

 8. At the very outset Advocate Mr. Sheikh Sirajul Islam representing the condemned-prisoner Md. Matiur Rahman submits that primary requirement of law as per the provision of Section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not fulfilled in producing the said accused before the court of Magistrate; that the confessional statement of the accused Md. Jahurul Haque is not true and voluntary; that the case was got up by the local salisders; that commission of rape on the victim was not proved in this case; that the condemned-accused-persons were not properly examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure; that the prosecution withheld vital witnesses in this case and as such, this accused is entitled to the benefit of the provision of Section 114(g) of the Evidence Act; that the prosecution could not prove its case beyond reasonable doubt against the condemned-prisoner Md. Matiur Rahman and as such, he is entitled to an order of acquittal in this case. The learned advocate also referred the decisions reported in 4 BLD(AD) at page 193, 4 BLT(AD) at page 107, 28 DLR at page 192, 60 DLR at page 457, 12 BLD(AD) at page 91, 13 BLD at page 277 and 17 BLD at page 15. 

 11. On the other hand, Mr. Bhishmadeb Chakraborty, the learned Deputy Attorney General (DAG) appearing on behalf of the State submits that the learned trial court was well-founded in law in convicting and sentencing the accused-persons on the basis of the evidences on record; that the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence does not warrant interference by this court and it should be upheld and confirmed. He prays for acceptance of the death reference. The learned DAG also referred the decisions reported in 39 DLR(AD) at page 117, 39 DLR (AD) at page 164 and 16 DLR at page 164. 

 12. In order to appreciate the respective arguments of the learned Advocates, we would not discuss the evidence adduced by the prosecution in this case. 

 26. The P.W.14 Md. Abdus Samad P.P.M.S.I stated in his deposition that on 24.12.1994 he was attached to Sapahar P.S. as an S.I. On that day after starting the case, the Officer-in-Charge Md. Nazir Hossain filled up the FIR Form and entrusted him with the charge of investigation of the case. During investigation he visited the place of occurrence, held inquest on the dead body of the diseased, prepared Inquest Report, seized alamats under a Seizure List, drew Sketch Map of the place of occurrence with Index, recorded the statements of the witnesses under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, arrested the accused-persons Md. Jahurul Haque and Matiur Rahman. On query, the accused-persons admitted to him that after committing rape on the victim Ribina they killed her. He sent the accused-persons for recording their confessional statements. The accused Juhurul Haque made confessional statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. After investigation prima-facie case having been made out against the accused-persons he submitted Memorandum of Evidence for approval to submit Charge Sheet. In the mean time, due to his transfer elsewhere he handed the docket of the case over to the Officer-in-Charge. This witness proved the FIR and the signature of the Officer-in-Charge there, the Inquest Report and his signature therein, the Seizure List in respect of the gauge scarf, the Seizure List, in respect of the money, the Chalan of the dead body (Exhibit-5) and his signature therein (Exhib,,-5/1), the Sketch Map (Exhibit-6) and his signature therein (Exhibit-6/1), the Index of the Sketch Map (Exhibit-7) and his signature therein (Exhibit-7/1). This witness also identified the alamats of the case in the court. In his cross this witness stated that he arrested the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur on 17.04.1995. He took the accused Matiur on remand for three days. On 19.05.1995 he submitted Memorandum of Evidence. This witness denied the defence-suggestion that one Rafiqul killed Ribina or that he deposed falsely. 

 27. The P.W.15 Inspector of Police Md. Ibrahim stated in his deposition that on 19.05.1995 he was attached to Sapahar Police Station as an S.I. On that date the case was endorsed to him for taking out the remaining investigation: The previous Investigating Officer submitted the Memorandum of Evidence to the higher authority after completing the investigation of the case for submission of charge-sheet. On 21.06 1995 having received the approval to submit the Charge Sheet, he submitted Charge Sheet No. 24 dated 21.06.1995 under Sections 376/302/34 of the Penal Code read with Section 7 of the Nario-O-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 1983. In his cross this witness stated that after perusing the papers he submitted charge sheet. This witness denied the defence-suggestion that the Charge Sheet as submitted by him was not a correct one. 

 28. So, these are the evidences adduced by the prosecution to substantiate its case. Now, on analysis and on scrutiny of the evidence on record, let us see as to whether the prosecution had been able beyond all shadow of doubt to substantiate the Charge as brought against the condemned-prisoner and the condemned-accused and so also find out whether the impugned judgment and order of conviction is sustainable in law. 

 29. The P.W.1, the informant Md. Altas Ali supported the prosecution case in his evidence. This witness stated in his evidence that the occurrence took place on 23.12.1994; that on that day at 6.00 p.m. the victim Ribina went to the religious meeting held in Kormudanga Rahmania Madrasah to sell boiled egg but the victim did not return; that that on 24.12.1994 at 7.00 a.m. the dead body of Ribina was seen lying in the field; that the neck of the victim Ribina was twisted with a gauge scarf, her salwar was open and that there was sign of bleeding form genital organ; that somebody committed rape on Ribina and killed her by twisting her throat with gauge scarf; that during investigation the Investigating Officer arrested the accused-Persons Jahurul Haque and Matiur Rahman who admitted that after committing rape on the victim they killed her by twisting her throat with gauge scarf; that the accused Jahurul Haque made confessional statement before a Magistrate and that the accused Matiur Rahman confesed his guilt to the Investigating Officer, that he did not see mark of assault on any other part of the body of Ribina excepting the genital organ. This witness denied the defence-suggestion that the accused-persons were not involved in the alleged occurrence or that he did not suspect the accused-persons. The P.W.2 Md. Emaj Uddin stated in his evidence that on the night of occurrence Ribina about 10/11 years of age went to sell boiled egg; that on the night of occurrence somebody took away Ribina and killed her by committing rape on her: that Jahurul and Matiur were the accused-persons in this case; that the enquiry committee of the locality handed over the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur to police. The P.W.3 Mosammat Golenur Bibi stated in her evidence that on the night of occurrence the victim Ribina 10/11 years of age went to sell out boiled egg in the Madrasah field where a religious meeting was held but she did not return; that that on the following morning the dead body of Ribina was found in the field; that the dead body of Ribina was naked; that her frock was raised over her chest; that blood came out from the genital organ of Ribina; that she was killed after commission of rape on her; that she heard that Jahurul, Rafique, Samjad committee rape on Ribina and killed her; that the members of the local enquiry committee handed the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur to the police to be the perpetrator of the alleged occurrence; that the accused Jahurul made confessional statement to a Magistrate; This witness denied the defence-suggestions that Rafique and Samjad killed Ribina after committing rape on her or that she did not see blood in the genital organ of Ribina. The P.W.4 Md. Saiful Islam stated in his evidence that the occurrence took place on 23.12.1994 after dusk; that on the night of occurrence the victim Ribina about 10/11 years of age went to sell boiled egg at the religious meeting held at Rahmania Madrasha field; that in the following morning the dead body of Ribina was found in naked condition in the field; that her throat was twisted with a gauge scarf; that there was blood in her genital organ; that after committing rape on her she was killed; that the accused-persons Matiur Rahman and Jahurul took away Ribina, committed rape on her and killed her; that after the occurrence that accused-persons Matiur Rahman and Jahurul went in hiding; that the accused Jahurul admitted his guilt. This witness denied the defence-suggestion that he deposed falsely. The P.W.5 Md. Alam stated in his evidence that on the date of occurrence the victim Ribina was selling boiled egg at the religious meeting held at the Rahmania Madrasha on the night of occurrence; that on the following morning the heard that the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur killed Ribina; that the dead body of Ribina was lying in the open field. This witness denied the defence-suggestion that the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur did not kill Ribina or that the deposed falsely. The P.W.6 Md. Afser Ali Biswas stated in is evidence that on 23.12.1994 at night the victim Ribina died; that hearing that the dead body of Ribina was lying in the field he went there to see that her throat was twisted with a gauge scarf and that she was naked; that the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur remained absconding after the date of occurrence; that the accused Jahurul made confessional statement to a Magistrate; that Ribina was killed after committing rape on her; that first of all the accused Jahurul committed rape on the victim and as a result, blood came out from her genital organ; that thereafter, when the accused Matiur went to commit rape seeing the critical condition of the victim twisted her throat and as a result, she died. The P.W.7 Md. A. Rahim stated in is evidence that the occurrence took place 11 years back on Friday at night; that on the night of occurrence his daughter, the victim Ribina 11 years of age went to the religious meeting held at Rahmania Madrasha to sell boiled egg; that on that night Ribina was not found on search; that on the following morning the dead body of Ribina was found in the field of Madrasha; that he saw that the frock of his daughter was raised above the chest; that she was naked; that blood came out from her genital organ; that Ribina was killed by twisting her throat with gauge scarf after committing rape on her; that the accused Jahurul and Matiur killed Ribina by committing rape on her; that the accused Jahurul made statement to a Magistrate confessing his guilt. This witness denied the defence-suggestion that Afser Biswas and Tobarak implicated the accused Jahirul in the case. The P.W.8 Mosammat Kadon Bibi stated in her evidence that the occurrence took place 11 years back on Friday at night; that on that night her daughter Ribina went to the religious meeting held in the field of Rahmania Madrasha to sell out boiled eggs; that thereafter, Ribina was not found; that in the following morning the dead body of Ribina was found in the land of Sohrab chairman; that after going to the place of occurrence she saw that Ribina was lying in naked condition; that her frock was raised above the chest; that her throat was twisted with a gauge scarf and that blood came out due to commission of rape on her; that the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur committed rape on Ribina and killed her; that the throat of Ribina was tied up tightly with gauge scarf. The P.W.9 Maulvi Kutubuddin Bhuiyan stated in his evidence that the occurrence took place 11 years back on the 9'' day of Poush on Friday at night; that on that day a religious meeting was held at Kormudanga Rahmania Madrasha which ended at 12 '0' clock at night; that in the following morning while he was going to his house he saw the dead body of the deceased Ribina; that the frock of Ribina was raised above her chest and that she was lying; that Ribina was killed by twisting her throat with gauge scarf; that the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur committed rape on the victim Ribina and killed her. This witness denied the defence-suggestion that Ribina saw Rafiqul to commit rape on Samjan or that Rafiqul killed Ribina. The P.W.10 Md. Imtazul stated in his evidence that the occurrence took place 11/12 years back on Friday at night; that in the following morning the dead body of Ribina was found in the field; that Ribina went to sell boiled egg in the religious meeting at Rahmania Madrasha wherefrom she was taken away and killed; that he heard that the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur killed her. This witness denied the defence-suggestion that he did not hear that the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur killed Ribina. The P.W.11 Ataur Rahman stated in his evidence that the occurrence took place 11 years back on Friday at night; that Ribina went to sell boilded eggs at the religious meeting of Rahmania Madrasha but she did not return home; that in the following morning the dead body of Ribina was found in the Kormudanga field; that the dead body of Ribina was lying naked; that the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur admitted to have killed Ribina. This witness denied the defence-suggestion that Ribina saw Rafiqul to commit rape on Samjan or that Rafiqul killed Ribina. The P.W.12 Md. Jahangir Alam stated in his evidence that the occurrence took place 11/12 years back on Friday at night; that he along with Ribina went to sell boiled egg at the religious meeting of Rahmania Madrasha; that in the following morning the dead body of Ribina was found in the Kormudanga field situated to the north of the Madrasha; that the accused-persons Jahurul and Matiur committed rape on Ribina and killed her and that they confessed their guilt; that he made statement to the Investigating Officer. The P.W.8 Md. Shahidul Islam, Magistrate class stated in his evidence that on 19.04.1995 he was attached to Naogaon collectorate as a Magistrate 1' class; that on that day he recorded the confessional statement of the accused Md. Jahurul Haque; that after recording the statement he read over the statement to the accused to which he put his signature thereon admitting the contents thereof to be true; that the confessional statement as made by the accused Md. Jaurul Haque was voluntary and true; that the accused did not make any allegation of misbehaviour to him; that there was no mark of injury on the body of the accused; that he kept the accused-under the custody of his peon without handcuff for three hours. This witness denied the defence-suggestion that the confessional statement as made of the accused Md. Jahurul Haque was not true or voluntary. The P.W.14 S.I Abdus Samad stated in is evidence that on 24.12.1994 as per the oral version of the informant Altas Ali, the officer-in-Charge Md. Nazir Hossein started the case and filled up the FIR Form and endorsed the case to him for investigation; that during investigation he visited the place of occurrence, held inquest on the dead body of the diseased Ribina, seized alamats of the case, drew Sketch Map of the place of occurrence with Index, recorded the statements of the witnesses under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, arrested the accused-persons Md. Jahunil Haque and Md. Matiur Rahman who admitted to him that they committed rape on the victim Ribina and killed her; that the accused Jahurul Haque made confessional statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure; that after investigation prima-facie case having been made out against the accused-persons he submitted Memorandum of Evidence to submit Charge Sheet against them; that due to his transfer he handed the docket of the case over the Officer-in-Charge; that he submitted Memorandum of Evidence on 19.05.1995. The P.W.15 Inspector of Police Md. Ibrahim stated in his evidence that on 19.05.1995 he was attached to Sapahar Police Station as an S.I.; that on that date the case was endorsed to him for taking out the remaining investigation; that the previous Investigating Officer submitted the Memorandum of Evidence seeking permission to submit the Charge Sheet of the case; that on 21.06.1995 having received the permission to submit the charge Sheet of the case he submitted charge sheet no. 24 dated 21.06.1995 under Sections 376/302/34 of the Penal Code read with Section 7 of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983. This witness denied the defence-suggestion the Charge Sheet as submitted by him was not a correct one. From the evidence of the PW14 and the PW 15, the Investigating Officers, they appear not to have committed any illegality or irregularity in taking out investigation of the case. 

 30. On analysis and on perusal of the evidence of the prosecution witnesses, it appears that on the night of occurrence the accused Md. Jahurul Haque committed rape on the victim Ribina pressing his mouth and that the accused Md. Matiur Rahman assisted him in doing so; that due to commission of rape by the accused Md. Jahurul Haque while the victim was crying out in pain then the accused Md. Matiur Rahman twisted the throat of the victim Ribina with her gauge scarf and as a result, she died of strangulation and asphyxia and that the prosecution case finds support from the evidence of the prosecution witnesses. 

 31. Apart from the aforesaid evidence of the prosecution witnesses there is the confessional statement of the condemned-accused Md. Jahurul Haque in this case. Said accused stated in his confessional statement that on the date and at the time of occurrence he first started committing rape on the victim Ribina; that due to commission of rape when the victim kept crying in pain he asked the condemned-prisoner Matiur to gag her mouth; that he again asked the condemned-prisoner Matiur to twist the throat of Ribina; that Matiur twisted the throat of Ribina with her gauge scarf and he himself also gagged her mouth; that due to commission of rape Ribina bleeded from her genital organ; that thereafter, they left the victim girl behind in 

 32. On perusal of the confessional statement of the condemned-accused Md. Jahurul Haque, it transpires that he made the statement implicating himself and so also implicating the condemned-prisoner Md. Matiur Rahman directly in the alleged occurrence. As stated earlier, the pwl3 Md. Shahidul Islam Magistrate 1" class stated in his evidence that after recording the confessional statement he read it over to accused Md. Jahurul Haque to which he put his signature therein admitting the contents thereof to be true; that the confessional statement as made by the accused Md. Jahurul Haque was voluntary and true; that the accused Md. Jahurul Haque did not make any allegation of misbehaviour to him; that there was no make of injury on the body of the accused. 

 33. In view of the discussion made so far, there is no difficulty to come to a finding that the confessional statement (Exhibit-4) as made by the condemned-accused Md. Jahurul Haque is true, inculpatory and voluntary and it may well form the basis for conviction of the accused-persons. It is the established principle of law that judicial confession if it is found to be true and voluntary can form the sole basis of conviction against the maker of the same (Reference; the case of Islamuddin (Md.) versus The State reported in 13 BLC (AD) at page 81). It is also the settled principle of law that once a confession has been found to be true and voluntary, conviction can be based solely on the basis of the confession, even if it is retracted (Reference: the case of Bakul Chandra Sarker reported in 45 DLR at page 260). In his confessional statement the accused Md. Jahurul Haque implicated the accused Md. Matiur Rahman directly in the alleged occurrence stating specifically as to what role he played in the alleged occurrence. In this regard the learned DAG referred the cases of State versus Lalu Miah and another reported in 39 DLR(AD)at page 117 and the case of Nausher All Sarder and others versus The State reported in 39 DLR(AD) at page 194. In the case of State versus Lalu Miah and another reported in reported in 39 DLR(AD) at page 117 our apex court held that Section 30 of the Evidence Act provides for consideration that a confession made by one of such persons affecting himself and some other of such persons being jointly tried and the Court may take into consideration such confession as against such other person as well as against the person who makes such confession. The explanation says offence includes the abetment of or attempt to commit the offence. In the case of Nausher Ali Sarder & others versus The state reported in 39 DLR(AD) at page 194 our apex court held that as per the provision of the Section 30 of the evidence Act, 1872 confession when proved against confessing accused can be taken into consideration against co-accused in the same offence. In this case the confessional statement of the accused Md. Jahurul Haque has been well proved against him. It has already been stated earlier that the confessing accused stated categorically what role the accused Md. Matiur Rahman played in the alleged ocurrence. In this case most of the prosecution witnesses stated in their evidence that the accused Md. Jahurul Haque and the accused Md. Matiur Rahman raped and killed the victim Ribina. The prosecution witnesses stated in their evidence that when the dead body of the victim Ribina was found they saw that her throat was twisted and tied up with a gauge scarf which supports the averment of the confessing accused Md. Jahurul Haque in his confessional statement that at the time of commission of rape by him on victim Ribina the accused Md. Matiur Rahman twisted the throat of Ribina with her gauge scarf. In the Inquest Report (Exhibit-2), it is stated that the throat of the victim Ribina was twisted and tied up with a gauge scarf and that the mark of strangulation was seen there. In the Post Mortem Examination Report (Exhibit-8), it is stated that cause of death of the deceased was due to asphyxia as a result of strangulation which was ante mortem and homicidal in nature and signs of sexual violence was present. In this case the Inquest Report, the Post Mortem Examination Report and the confessional statement of the accused Md. Jahurul Haque are consistent with each other. In this case it is proved to the hilt that the condemned-prisoner Md. Matiur Rahman facilitated the accused Md. Jahurul Haque to commit rape on the victim and that he was an abettor and participant in the alleged occurrence. This court, therefore, is in respectful agreement with the aforesaid decisions of our Apex Court. In this case the condemned-accused Md. Jahurul Haque filed an application for retraction of his confessional statement on 16.05.1995 long one month after making confessional statement which is nothing but a product of afterthought and as such, it cannot be accepted. The learned Advocate Mr. Sheikh Muhammed Serajul Islam representing the condemned-prisoner Md. Matiur Rahman submits that the condemned-accused Md. Jahurul Haque being not produced before the Magistrate court within 24 hours from the time of his arrest as per the provisions of sections 61 and 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure his confessional statement cannot be taken into consideration. On the other hand, the learned DAG submits that considering the facts and circumstances of the case the condemned-accused was produced before the court of Magistrate within 24 hours from the time of his arrest. The learned DAG also referred the case of State versus Ali Ahmed reported in 16 DLR at page 558. As per Section 61 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, an arrested person is to be produced before the Magistrate court within 24 hours of arrest exclusive of the time necessary for the journey. Each case of this nature has to be judged on its own merits upon a very careful scrutiny of all the facts of the case. On perusal of the Case Diary (CD) of the case, it transpires that a break up has been given therein from the arrest of the condemned-accused Md. Jahurul Haque till his production before the court of Magistrate. On perusal of the Case Diary, it transpires that on 18.04.1995 at 9.55 a.m. the accused-persons Md. Matiur Rahman and Md. Jahurul Haque were produced in the Police Station after their arrest; that the accused-persons Md. Jahurul Haque and Md. Matiur Rahman admitted to have committed rape on the victim Ribina and killed her to police on interrogation; that in view of the admission of the accused-persons the Investigating Officer kept making arrangement for getting recorded the confessional statements of the accused-persons; that the accused persons also admitted their guilt to the Officer-in-Charge and that the Officer-in-Charge advised him (the Investigating Officer) to take necessary steps to that effect; that the Investigating Officer interrogated the accused-persons to ascertain as to whether any other persons was involved in the alleged occurrence to which they replied that none else other than they were involved in the alleged occurrence; that it would be dusk to send the accused-persons to the court and that after dusk recording of the confessional statement of the accused-persons under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was not possible and that was why the Investigating Officer started for the court from the Police station on 19.04.1995 at 9.25 a.m. and reached the court at 11.30 a.m. and produced the accused-persons before the court at 12.00 '0' clock at noon and the confessional statement of the accused Md. Jahurul Haque was recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In this case, admittedly the distance of the Naogaon head quarter from Sapahar Police Station is 40 kilometre. On perusal of the confessional statement of the condemned-accused Md. Jahurul Haque, it appears that he did not make any complaint of maltreatment or torture on him or pressure put to him or inducement given to him by police to the Magistrate who recorded the confessional statement on him before making the confessional statement. Be it mentioned here that In this case the accused Md. Jahurul Haque remained in abscondence through out the trial without facing it. It has already been stated earlier that in this case the condemned —accused Md. Jahurul Haque filed an application, for retraction of his confessional statement on 16.05.1995 long one month after making confessional statement which is nothing but a product of afterthought. It has been already found that the confessional statement as made by the condemned-accused Md. Jahurul Haque is true, inculpatory and voluntary. In view of the discussion made so far this court finds nothing on record to suspect that the confessional statement of the condemned-accused Md. Jahurul Haque was in any way influenced by police or that it has in any way affected the confessional statement. In the case of State versus Ali Ahmed reported in 16 DLR at page 558 it is held that there being no complaint from the accused about any torture, threat or any inducement by the police to the Magistrate nothing was there to suspect the confessional statement of the accused recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure although the accused was produced before the Court of Magistrate after 24 hours. It is also held that the conduct of the Investigating officer in not observing the mandate as laid down in section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has in any way affected the confessional statement. 

 34. In this case the prosecution could not produce the doctor who held Post Mortem Examination on the dead body of the deceased and that the Post Mortem examination report was admitted in evidence after exhausting all procedures to secure his attendance in the trial court as per the provision of Section 509A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. So, there was no illegality or irregularity in taking the Post Mortem Examination Report into consideration by the trial court. It is the defence case that the condemned-prisoner and the condemned-accused did not commit rape on the victim Ribina or killed her, rather, one Rafiqul Islam took away Ribina, committed rape on her and killed her on the apprehension that Ribina might disclose the fact of committing rape on one Samjan by said Rafiqul Islam. But to substantiate said contention, the defence did not adduce any evidence or did not make any attempt to prove it. At one stage of her submission the learned Advocate Mrs. Hasna Begum representing the condemned-prisoner Md. Matiur Rahman in Jail Appeal No 551 of 2006 submits that there is no eye witness with regard to the commission of rape on the deceased. But no offence of rape is committed in presence of any witness. The learned Advocate Mr. sheikh Muhammed Serajul Islam submits that that commission of rape on the victim was not proved in this case and that the prosecution withheld the vital witnesses in this case and as such, this accused in entitled to the benefit of the provision of Section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. In this case there was no denial even from the defence that the victim was not raped or not killed after committing rape on her. No specific denial to that effect from the side of the defence even was given to the prosecution witnesses. Further, it is for the prosecution to decide amongst the cited witnesses in the prosecution report how many it will examine for establishing its case against the accused-persons placed on trial (Reference: the case of Zahed Ali Foreman (Driver) and others versus The State reported in 9 BLC(AD) at page 123) as to how many or which witness it would examine. It is also worth mentioning that in the case the date of occurrence, the time of occurrence and the place of occurrence was not challenged on behalf of the defence. So, the said submission of the learned Advocate does not stand. 

 35. In this case, from the evidence on record, it is found that after the occurrence the condemned-accused-persons absconded which is a fact points to their guilt in the alleged occurrence. So, from the Inquest Report, the Post Mortem Examination Report, the confessional statement of the accused Md. Jahurul Haque, the evidence of the prosecution witnesses and the circumstantial evidence, it is crystal clear that the victim was raped and killed by the condemned-prisoner and the condemned-accused and that the prosecution could prove its case beyond all shadow of doubt. 

 37. In the light of discussion made here above, and so also on consideration of the evidence on record, facts and circumstances of the case and so also on observation of the decisions as cited by the learned Advocates we find that the learned trial Judge was perfectly justified in passing the impugned judgment and order. This court also finds that the learned trial court rightly awarded death sentence to the condemned-accused Md. Zahurul Haque. In this case there is no mitigating or extenuating circumstances in favour of the condemned-accused Md. Jahurul Haque in view of the brutality and gruesomeness with which the victim Ribina was killed. In this regard we may refer the case of Md. Ershad Ali Sikder versus The State reported in 9 MLR(AD) at page 355) in which our apex court held that the sentence of death is the appropriate where the death is caused with extreme brutality.But considering the facts, circumstances and evidence on record, the death sentence as awarded to the condemned-prisoner Md. Matiur Rahman seems to this court to be harsh and as such, this court is inclined to commute the death sentence as awarded to the condemned-prisoner Md. Matiur Rahman. This court thinks that justice will be amply not if the condemned-prisoner Md. Matiur Rahman is sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Tk. 10.000/00, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for another 6(six) months on commutation of the death sentence as awarded to him.
